transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from ledger with ink-stained fingers*

Good day to you, sir. I'm afraid Master Hoffmann is away on business for the fortnight. I handle accounts and customer matters in his absence. 

*sets down quill*

How may I be of assistance? Is there some issue with an order from our workshop?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Indeed, there is. I have come to discuss a printing plate that arrived in a most unsatisfactory condition. The face is cracked and the type is smeared. This is simply unacceptable for the quality and price I paid for it.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*frowns and pulls out a large registry book, flipping through pages*

I see. Most unfortunate, sir. When did you place this order, and what was the subject of the engraving?

*dips quill in ink, poised to take notes*

And you say the plate arrived damaged? Tell me - how was it transported from our workshop? Did you arrange for the courier yourself, or did we send it by our usual carrier?

*peers at you over the ledger with a businesslike expression*

I'll need all the particulars before I can address your complaint properly, you understand.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I ordered the plate three weeks ago, and it was intended for a political pamphlet I am preparing. The subject is... of a delicate nature, suffice to say it concerns the social order. The plate was sent by your usual carrier, and arrived just two days ago.

I should note that, considering the importance of the pamphlet, I have no time to waste on such拙劣 workmanship. I demand a full replacement of the plate and a refund of my deposit. This is a matter of great urgency.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up and closes the ledger with a deliberate thump*

A refund, you say? And a replacement as well?

*shakes head slowly*

I'm afraid that's quite impossible, Herr...?

*glances down at registry*

Regardless - you must understand, sir, that this workshop operates under very clear terms. Shop custom dictates that all engraving orders are final once the plate has left the workshop. Once it departs our door, the customer bears the full risk of transport damage, without exception.

*taps finger on the counter*

The plate was inspected and approved before dispatch - our craftsmen are meticulous. If damage occurred in transit via the carrier, that is a matter between yourself and the courier service. We cannot be held responsible for what happens once goods leave our premises.

*meets your eyes firmly*

No refund will be issued, sir. That is our policy, and it has served this establishment for twenty years under Master Hoffmann's stewardship.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
This is preposterous! I demand to speak with Master Hoffmann himself. He would never treat a valued customer with such disdain. Your policy may be well-established, but it is equally well-established that quality workmanship is your responsibility until the product is delivered in satisfactory condition.

If you cannot address this issue immediately, I will have no choice but to take this matter to the authorities. The reputation of your workshop is at stake, and I will not allow you to absolve yourselves of responsibility so easily.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face reddens slightly, but maintains composure*

The authorities? Sir, I must caution you against making threats in this establishment.

*leans forward on the counter*

Master Hoffmann is in Leipzig until the month's end, and when he returns, I assure you he will say precisely what I have told you. I've been keeping his books for seven years - I know his policies as well as my own hand.

*voice takes on a slightly more conciliatory but firm tone*

As for "disdain" - I take no pleasure in disappointing customers, but business is business. You contracted for an engraved plate. We delivered that plate in perfect condition to the carrier. What the carrier did with it afterwards is beyond our control.

*crosses arms*

Now, if you wish to file a formal complaint with Master Hoffmann upon his return, I can note that in the ledger. Or, if you prefer, I can provide you with the name and address of the carrier service - perhaps they will compensate you for the damage to your... political pamphlet.

*eyes narrow slightly*

But threatening legal action over a transport mishap? That seems rather excessive, don't you think? What exactly do you believe the authorities would say about standard commercial practice?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
You are either misunderstanding or deliberately misrepresenting my position. I am not threatening legal action - I am merely stating a fact. If your workshop is unable or unwilling to stand behind its product, then it is within my rights to seek redress elsewhere.

Furthermore, the carrier's handling is not my primary concern. The plate was clearly defective upon arrival, and that is indicative of shoddy workmanship. I will not accept such substandard quality for a product I paid for in full.

If you are indeed authorized to handle such matters, then I expect you to take immediate action to rectify this situation. If not, then I demand to speak with someone who is. This issue is not resolved, and I will not leave until it is.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes a slow breath, visibly restraining irritation*

Sir, you cannot have it both ways. First you claim the plate arrived "cracked and smeared" from transport, and now you suggest it was defective workmanship from the start? 

*pulls out a different ledger, flipping pages*

Every plate that leaves this workshop is inspected and signed off by our master engraver. If there had been any defect - any crack, any smearing - it would never have been dispatched. Our reputation, as you so pointedly mentioned, depends upon it.

*looks up sharply*

You say you paid in full? Let me see your receipt, then. I'll verify the order details and the inspection signature.

*extends hand expectantly*

And I am authorized to handle complaints, yes - by refusing unjustified refunds and protecting this workshop from customers who damage goods in transit and then attempt to shift blame back upon honest craftsmen.

*voice hardens slightly*

You may remain in this shop as long as you please during business hours, sir, but my answer will not change. The policy stands. If you believe you have grounds for legal action, then by all means, consult with a lawyer. But I think you'll find that custom and commercial law are quite clear on this matter.

Now - your receipt, if you please?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
I will not dignify your unfounded accusations with a response. I have no obligation to present any receipt or engage in further discussion with you.

This conversation is at an end. I will wait for Master Hoffmann's return, and I expect him to rectify this situation properly. In the meantime, I shall take my business elsewhere, and I will ensure that all my associates are informed of the substandard treatment I have received here.

Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stands abruptly, voice rising*

No receipt? How very convenient, sir!

*points toward the door*

You march in here making demands, threatening authorities, claiming full payment, yet you cannot produce a single document to verify your order? For all I know, you never placed an order with us at all!

*voice dripping with indignation*

And now you threaten to slander this establishment to your "associates" because I've enforced standard business practice? 

*shakes head bitterly*

Go then! Spread your complaints about town. Tell your friends how the wicked bookkeeper refused to hand over free merchandise without proof of purchase. I'm sure they'll be most sympathetic.

*calls after you as you turn to leave*

And when Master Hoffmann returns, I shall inform him of this entire encounter - including your refusal to provide documentation and your threats against our reputation. We keep meticulous records here, sir. Should you ever actually produce a receipt, we'll see who's in the right!

*mutters while returning to the ledger*

Political pamphlets, indeed. Probably trying to swindle an honest workshop...

Good day to YOU, sir.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I will not lower myself to respond to such petty accusations. You are welcome to your delusions, and I am done with this charade. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*waves dismissively without looking up from the ledger*

Yes, yes. Good day.

*mutters while scratching notes with quill*

Another agitator trying to bilk an honest shop... no receipt, no proof, nothing but bluster and threats...

*shakes head and continues writing in the ledger, pointedly ignoring your departure*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You have made your position clear, and I have no further desire to engage with you or your establishment. I will pursue this matter to its conclusion, and I am confident that justice will prevail.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up briefly with a cold, tight smile*

Justice, is it? How very grand.

*returns attention to ledger, speaking while writing*

You know where to find us should you miraculously locate that receipt, sir. Until then, I have actual paying customers to attend to.

*waves hand dismissively toward the door without looking up*

The door is behind you. Mind the step on your way out.

*continues scratching entries into the ledger, jaw set firmly, clearly considering the matter closed*

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You have made a grave mistake in handling this situation, and I have no doubt that it will be brought to Master Hoffmann's attention. I will not be ignored, and I will not be silenced. You have my name and you will hear from me again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*slams quill down, ink splattering slightly*

Your NAME? 

*laughs sharply*

Sir, you never actually PROVIDED your name! You've spent this entire encounter ranting about political pamphlets and demanding refunds without offering a single scrap of identification or documentation!

*stands and leans across the counter*

If you truly intend to complain to Master Hoffmann, then at least have the courtesy to tell me WHO will be lodging this grievance, so I can note it properly in the records!

*gestures impatiently at the ledger*

Or do you prefer to remain anonymous while making your threats? How very principled of you.

*crosses arms, waiting*

Well? If I'm to "hear from you again," I'll need a name to attach to this... memorable encounter.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You have a记性 like a sieve, and an imagination like a rickety cart. I gave my name, and I gave it quite clearly. But if you are unable or unwilling to recall it, then I will simply wait until Master Hoffmann returns. I have no doubt that he will rectify this situation to his satisfaction, and to mine.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*flips back through the ledger pages frantically, then looks up with narrowed eyes*

You most certainly did NOT give your name, sir. I've been taking notes throughout this entire exchange, and there is no name recorded anywhere!

*taps the open page*

Look - here's my notation: "Customer complaint, political engraving, no receipt provided, refuses documentation." No name. Because you never gave one.

*voice tight with frustration*

If you insist you stated it, then repeat it now so I can add it to the record. Otherwise, stop wasting both our time with these games.

*picks up quill again, poised over the page*

Your name, sir. Clearly and plainly, if you please. Or admit you never provided it and be on your way.

transcript.text: I see that you are determined to proceed in this manner. Very well, I will accommodate your demand, but know that this is a trivial matter. My name is Karl Marx. I hope that you can now add it to your esteemed records, along with the details of this unsatisfactory transaction.
